*The Part Nobody Else Shows You*

## You can't fix a leak you can't see.

Most business owners are guessing. They know roughly how many leads come in and roughly how many turn into money — and everything in between is a black box. Your AI employees measure every step, so the leak stops being a mystery and starts being a number you can fix.

STEP 01

Lead arrives

Where it came from, what they asked for, and the exact second it landed.

STEP 02

First response

How fast you actually replied — measured in seconds, not "pretty quick."

STEP 03

Follow-up

Every touch sent, and which one finally got a reply.

STEP 04

Booked

How many conversations became appointments on the calendar.

STEP 05

Showed up

Your real show rate — booked is not the same as held.

STEP 06

Won

Which leads turned into revenue, and what that revenue was worth.

STEP 07

Reviewed

Who was asked for a review, and who actually left one.

STEP 08

Referred

Which happy customers sent you the next one.

**This is the difference between marketing and guessing.** When you can see that leads stall at step two, or that half your booked appointments never show, you stop throwing money at more leads and start fixing the step that's actually costing you. You see all of it in your own dashboard — not a report we email you once a month.

*Questions*

## The stuff everyone asks

**Will it sound like a robot?**

No. During setup we train your AI employee on your voice, your services, and your way of talking to customers. Most customers never realize they weren't texting the owner.

**What if it says something wrong?**

You choose the control level. Drafts wait for your approval. Recommendations wait for your tap. Only low risk actions like posting scheduled content run on their own, and you set those rules upfront.

**Do I need any tech skills?**

Zero. Setup is fully done for you. If you can tap approve on your phone, you can run your AI employees.

**What kind of businesses does this work for?**

Any business that lives on leads and reputation. Salons, med spas, contractors, realtors, gyms, clinics, restaurants, coaches. If customers call, message, or Google you, this works.

**Is there a contract?**

Month to month. We keep clients because the AI employees keep working, not because a contract traps you.

What she actually does

## You don't need a chatbot. You need the first five minutes handled.

Every lead gets the same treatment your best salesperson gives on their best day. Then your best salesperson gets the booking.

01 · Answer

### Replies before they've put the phone down

The leak: the reply that came six hours late.

Jessica answers in seconds, in your business's voice, with your services and your pricing rules. She's an AI and upfront about it: by text, chat and DM she says so in her first message, and on a call she tells anyone who asks.

02 · Qualify

### One question at a time, like a person

The leak: the form nobody fills out and the intake call nobody has time for.

She asks what they need, how urgent it is, what they've tried. She mirrors their words. The goal is understanding the problem, not filling a spreadsheet.

03 · Handle the objection

### "Let me think about it" isn't the end

The leak: the lead who went quiet and the follow-up you never sent.

She asks what specifically they'd want to think over. Usually it's one answerable thing. She offers to hold a slot they can cancel by text. She never pesters, and she stops the moment someone says stop.

04 · Book, then hand off

### Two concrete times, not "want to book?"

The leak: the "sounds good, I'll reach out" that nobody reaches out on.

She offers real openings from your calendar and locks it in the moment they pick. The appointment lands with a note on what they said. From there, a human owns the deal. That rule doesn't bend.

SMS Phone Instagram DM Facebook Messenger Email WhatsApp Website chat

One conversation per person. Someone who starts on Instagram and switches to text keeps the same thread.

Common questions

## Straight answers

**Does Jessica pretend to be a person?**

Never. Jessica is an AI. By text, chat and DM she says so in her first message. On a call she greets people with her name and your business name, and if anyone asks whether she's a real person, she tells the truth right away and offers a human. She never claims to be human.

**Does she run the sales call?**

No. She works the conversation up to a booked appointment. A human owns the deal from the moment it's on the calendar. That's our rule for every client, including us.

**Which channels does she cover?**

Text, phone, Instagram DMs, Facebook Messenger, email, WhatsApp and website chat. It's one conversation per person across all of them, so nobody repeats themselves.

**Does she send cold messages?**

No. Jessica only replies to people who contacted the business first or gave written consent. No purchased lists, no blasts. Anyone who texts STOP never hears from her again.

**Will she sound like my business or like a bot?**

She's trained on your services, your pricing rules, your qualifying questions and your FAQs. You can name her whatever fits your brand. You approve messages until you trust her, and anything she shouldn't handle gets handed to a person with a note.

**What does it cost?**

We price it on the call, on the leak she plugs, not on the software. If you'd rather have your numbers before that conversation, run the scorecard first.

## You are sitting on money you already paid for.

Every business we look at has the same asset gathering dust: a list of past customers and old quotes. People who called, who bought, who liked the work — and then just drifted. Nobody followed up, because following up is the thing that never makes it to the top of the day.

Meanwhile you're being sold more leads. New leads cost money and start from zero trust. The people on your list already cleared both bars. They're the cheapest revenue available to you, and almost nobody works them.

The First 10 is us proving that, on your actual list, in thirty days — before you ever commit to anything ongoing.

## How it works

Three steps. Almost none of them are yours.

1

### You hand us the list

Export it, screenshot it, or give us access — past customers, old quotes, dead leads. Fifteen minutes of your time, once.

2

### We clean it and work it

We scrub duplicates and bad numbers, segment by how they last engaged, then our AI employees call, text, and follow up in your voice. You approve the messaging before anything sends.

3

### Appointments hit your calendar

Booked directly into your schedule with reminders attached, so they actually show. You watch it happen in real time — not in a report at the end of the month.

If we're waiting on you, the clock pauses — we don't run it while you're busy, and we don't hold you to a deadline we can't control.

## Questions people actually ask

**Won't reaching out to old customers annoy them?**

It's the most common worry and it's almost always wrong. These people chose you once. A short, human message that sounds like you — not a blast — reads as good service, not spam. You approve the messaging before a single one sends, and anyone who asks to be left alone is removed immediately and permanently.

**Will it sound like a robot?**

The AI employees are trained on your business, your services, and how you actually talk to customers. Most people never realize they weren't texting your front desk. And you don't have to take our word for it — [talk to a live one right now](https://infinityreachmedia.com/live-demo) and try to stump it.

**What if my list is messy?**

Nearly all of them are. Duplicates, dead numbers, a spreadsheet somebody started three years ago. Cleaning and segmenting it is part of what you're paying for — hand it over however it exists.

**How much work is this for me?**

About fifteen minutes to hand over the list, then approving messaging before it goes out. That's the whole ask. We build it, we run it, you watch appointments appear.

**What happens after the 30 days?**

Entirely your call. Plenty of businesses run The First 10 and stop there — you keep the appointments and the revenue, no strings. If you'd rather keep it running and close the other leaks too, what you invested is credited toward your build fee and we talk about the ongoing partnership. There's no automatic enrollment and no contract. We'll give you the ongoing numbers on the call, once we know which leaks you actually need plugged.

**How is this different from the Dead List Miner on your pricing page?**

It's the same AI employee, working the same list. The First 10 is one concentrated 30-day sweep of a list nobody has touched in years, which is where the easy wins are. The ongoing Dead List Miner keeps mining a thinner seam every month after that — people who lapsed recently rather than years ago — which is why its written guarantee is ten in ninety days rather than ten in thirty. You're not buying two sets of ten. You're buying the sprint, and then deciding whether you want the machine that keeps it running.

**Why should I trust you with my customer list?**

Your data lives in accounts you own, not ours. We never sell, share, or reuse it, and you can revoke our access at any moment and keep everything. That's written into [our terms](https://infinityreachmedia.com/terms), not just promised on a page.

*The Honest Version*

# Most AI Agents Fail. Here's Exactly How.

Six ways it goes wrong — and the check that tells you which one is happening to you.

Everyone calls them AI agents. We call ours AI employees, because that is the bar they have to clear. We sell them, so you'd expect us to tell you they always work. They don't. Most of what gets sold to small businesses under the word "AI" fails in one of six predictable ways, and every one of them is visible before you sign anything — if you know what to look for.

No signup to read this. Nothing here is gated.

Nearly every failure below comes from the same root: *the AI employee was sold as a product instead of built as part of your business.* A product ships the same to everyone and hopes you make it fit. Six months later the seats renew and nobody logs in.

*The Six Failure Modes*

## If it's going wrong, it's one of these.

Each one gets a 30-second check you can run on your own business — or on whoever is pitching you — before any money moves.

01

### It answers confidently, and it's wrong

A generic chatbot with your logo on it doesn't know your hours, your service area, or what you actually charge. So it invents something plausible. You don't find out from a report — you find out from a customer who shows up expecting a price you never quoted.

**30-second check:** Ask the demo something only your business would know — a real price, a real policy, whether you cover a specific city. If it answers smoothly and wrongly, that's the failure mode, live.

**What we do instead:** Your AI employee is loaded with your services, your hours, your pricing rules, and the things you never want said on your behalf. When it gets something wrong, you correct it and the correction sticks. [Try to break ours →](https://infinityreachmedia.com/jessica)

02

### It sends something you'd never have sent

The scariest version of this isn't a typo. It's an automation emailing three hundred past customers at 2am in a voice that isn't yours, with an offer you didn't approve, and you learn about it from the replies.

**30-second check:** Ask who presses send. If the answer is "it's fully automated," ask what happens the first time it drafts something you'd be embarrassed by — and whether you'd see it before the customer does.

**What we do instead:** Approval mode is on from day one. Messages are drafted and wait for you — approve on your phone in a few taps. You can switch approval off later once you trust it, but that's your call to make, not a default we ship you into.

03

### It automates a process that was already broken

If leads go cold because nobody follows up, automating the follow-up fixes it. If they go cold because your intake asks the wrong questions, automation just makes the wrong questions arrive faster. Speed on a broken process gets you more of the same outcome, sooner.

**30-second check:** Ask them to name the step in your business they'd fix *before* switching anything on. If they can't — or if they don't ask about your process at all — they're selling you software, not a fix.

**What we do instead:** The Revenue Leak Score maps where the money is actually leaving before anyone talks about building. Sometimes the answer is that one AI employee fixes 80% of it and you don't need the rest yet. [Run your numbers free →](https://infinityreachmedia.com/scorecard)

04

### The data isn't yours, so you can't leave

Your customer list, your call history, your conversation records — the most valuable asset your business has — end up inside somebody else's platform. Leaving means starting over, so you don't leave, which is exactly what the pricing is counting on.

**30-second check:** Ask what you walk away with if you cancel next month. If there's hesitation, or the answer is "an export we can arrange," you're renting your own customer data.

**What we do instead:** Your data stays in your accounts, always. We build in your systems, not a walled garden you have to rent access to. Month to month, no contracts — the work has to be worth paying for every month, not just the month you signed.

05

### The demo was great. The rollout never happened.

The most common ending isn't a disaster — it's nothing. Something gets built, it half works, it needs your attention to finish, and your actual job takes priority. Six months later it's still 70% live and quietly costing you a subscription.

**30-second check:** Ask how many hours of *your* time it takes to go live, and what specifically happens if you don't have them that week.

**What we do instead:** Built, tested, and live within 7 days of your onboarding call — in writing, or your setup fee comes back. The clock only pauses when we're waiting on you, and it restarts the moment we have what we asked for. [Read the actual terms →](https://infinityreachmedia.com/terms#guarantees)

06

### Whoever sold it isn't whoever supports it

You buy from a senior person and get handed to a queue. When something needs changing — a price update, a new service, a message that's landing wrong — it becomes a ticket, and the person reading it has never spoken to you.

**30-second check:** Ask who you'll be talking to in month three, by name, and how many other clients that person is carrying.

**What we do instead:** We cap the client list at twelve. The people who scope your build are the people who build it and the people you call when something needs changing. That's only possible because of the cap — which is the whole reason for it.

---
title: "The Dead List Miner Playbook — Win Back Old Customers | Infinity Reach Media"
description: "The exact 5-message sequence, timing, and send rules we use to turn a business's old customer list into booked appointments — no discounts, no gimmicks. Free, nothing to sign up for."
url: "https://infinityreachmedia.com/reactivation-playbook"
---

## Start here: the list you already paid for

Every business has one — the spreadsheet, the CRM export, the invoices from two years ago. People who have already handed over money once and never came back. Nobody is calling them. Most owners assume they left for a reason.

They didn't. They got busy. The reason a past customer goes quiet is almost never dissatisfaction — it's that nothing ever reminded them. That's what makes this the cheapest revenue in the building: no ad spend, no lead cost, and a list that already recognises the name on the sender line.

Judge it on **replies, bookings, and revenue marked won** — not opens. Open tracking has been unreliable for years, and a win-back campaign lives or dies on whether real conversations start.

## Before a single message goes out

Most reactivation campaigns fail in the ten minutes before they're sent, not in the copy. Clear these five first.

- **Scrub the list.** Remove anyone who has ever unsubscribed, complained, or hard-bounced. One suppression list, checked automatically on every send, forever. Not optional, and not a nicety.
- **Remove current customers.** Nothing damages trust faster than "we miss you" landing in the inbox of somebody who bought last Tuesday.
- **Put the real physical address in the footer.** It's legally required on commercial email in the US, and it has to be the business's own address.
- **Point replies at a human.** Set reply-to to the owner's actual inbox. This sequence is built to get replies — catching them is the whole point.
- **Give it one destination.** One booking link, one phone number. If someone says yes, there should be exactly one obvious next step.

The pacing rule

Never send the whole list at once. 25 contacts a day for the first two days, then 40 a day once you've seen the bounce rate. An old list dumped in one batch is the fastest way to get every future email from that business — including invoices and password resets — filed as spam.

## The sequence

Five touches over fourteen days. Each does a different job, and the order matters: you earn the right to make an offer by making the first message about them. Day 0 is the day that contact's batch goes out, not a fixed calendar date.

Day 0

Email

### The check-in

No offer, no pitch, no discount. One job: prove a human noticed they were gone. This message earns more replies than any other in the sequence, and the warmest ones.

Subjectquick question, {{first_name}}

{{first_name}} — I was going back through our records this week and realised it's been a while since we last took care of you.

No pitch here. I'm genuinely curious whether we dropped the ball somewhere, or whether life just got busy. Either answer is useful to me.

If it's the second one, we're still here, and I'd love to have you back in.

**Why it works:** it asks a question a person can answer in four words. "Just got busy!" is a reply — and a reply is a live conversation you can book from.

Day 2

SMS · optional

### The nudge

Only to numbers that opted in to texts. One line, first name, signed by a person, always with an opt-out. If there's any doubt about consent, skip this touch entirely — the sequence works without it.

Hi {{first_name}}, it's {{owner_first_name}} at {{business}}. Sent you a note earlier this week — no pressure at all, just making sure it reached you. Reply STOP to opt out.

**Rule:** texts are held to a much stricter consent standard than email. Opted-in numbers only, business hours only, never a list you bought.

Day 4

Email

### The reason to come back

Now the offer — and it should be a reason, not a discount. Discounts teach a returning customer to wait for the next one and drag the whole list's price expectation down. Priority access, a seasonal check, a slot held back for them: all stronger than 20% off.

Subjectholding a spot for you

{{first_name}} — following up on my note.

We've opened up {{offer — e.g. pre-season inspection slots}} and I've kept a few back for people we've worked with before. Takes about {{duration}}, and most people find one thing they're glad they caught early.

If you'd like one, grab whatever time suits you here: {{booking_link}}

**Swap the offer, not the structure.** The shape — you're known to us, here's something specific, here's one link — is what carries. What's on offer changes by industry.

Day 8

Email

### The proof

Handles the silent objection: "is it still worth it?" One specific, verifiable story with a number in it. Not a testimonial wall — one customer, one problem, one outcome.

Subjectwhat we caught last week

Thought this was worth passing on, {{first_name}}.

{{customer_first_name}} booked in last week for the same thing I mentioned. We found {{specific finding}} — about {{$ amount}} to fix now, several times that if it had gone another season.

That's the whole reason we run these. Same link if you'd like a slot: {{booking_link}}

**Never invent this one.** Get a real story from the owner before the campaign starts. A fabricated case study is the fastest way to lose a list that already trusts the sender.

Day 12

Email

### The honest deadline

A real constraint, stated plainly. Real means it has to actually be true — the slots do run out, the season does end. Fake urgency gets noticed, and it gets remembered.

Subjectclosing these out {{day}}

Quick one, {{first_name}} — we're closing out the {{offer}} slots on {{day}}, and there are {{number}} left.

After that we're back to standard scheduling, which is usually a {{wait time}} wait this time of year.

If you want one: {{booking_link}}

**Watch:** if the deadline passes and the same offer reappears next week, the list learns your deadlines are decorative. Honour it.

Day 14

Email

### Permission to say no

The last message, and consistently the second-strongest replier in the sequence. Giving someone an easy exit is what makes answering feel safe — and a good share of the people who reply say the opposite of no.

Subjectshould I stop emailing?

{{first_name}}, I don't want to be the business that keeps emailing someone who's moved on.

If now isn't the time, just reply "not now" and I'll take you off this list — no hard feelings, and the door stays open whenever you need us.

And if the timing was just off, here's the link one last time: {{booking_link}}

**Honour the exit instantly.** Anyone who replies "not now" comes off the list that day and goes onto suppression permanently. That's what makes the ask sincere rather than a trick.

## Send rules that keep the list alive

Check these before each day's batch. They decide whether tomorrow's batch goes out at all.

| Signal | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bounces under 3% | Clean, current list | Carry on — you can raise the daily count |
| Bounces 3–5% | List is aging | Hold the pace, don't increase |
| Bounces over 5% | The data is stale, not the copy | Stop. Clean the list before sending again |
| Any spam complaint | Wrong message or wrong people | Stop and re-read the copy with the owner |
| Replies, no bookings | Interest is there, the ask isn't landing | Fix the Day 4 offer, keep the rest |

A high bounce rate is a **list** problem, not a sending problem. Pushing through it damages the sending reputation of every future email from that business — including invoices and receipts.

## What to do when they reply

This sequence is built to produce replies, so decide in advance who handles them and how fast. Speed is the whole game — a reply answered in minutes converts far better than one answered the next morning.

1. **Interested.** Don't sell. Send the booking link and one sentence: "Perfect — grab whatever time suits you here."
2. **Question or objection.** Answer it in one short message and offer a specific time. Never re-open the pitch.
3. **Not now.** Suppress immediately, reply once to thank them. That's a future customer, not a lost one.
4. **Annoyed.** Suppress, apologise once, no defence — then check how they ended up on the list.

Track one number

Revenue marked won, per campaign. Not opens, not clicks. When someone from the list books and pays, write the amount down against the campaign. That single number tells you whether to run the list again in ninety days — and it usually says yes.

## Running it on repeat

A list isn't spent after one pass. Anyone who didn't reply — and didn't opt out — can be worked again in about ninety days with a different angle: a seasonal reason, a new service, a genuine change in the business. Everyone who booked comes off the win-back list and into normal follow-up.

Done by hand, this is roughly an hour a day: split the list, write the batch, watch the bounces, catch the replies. That hour is exactly the part that gets dropped in week two — which is why most reactivation campaigns die halfway through. Not because the messages stopped working.

*This is the manual version*

## Or let the AI employee run it

The Dead List Miner drafts each batch in your voice, checks every address against your suppression list, paces the sends, watches the bounce rate, and routes replies to a human — and you approve every campaign before a single message goes out.

Book a 15-minute call and we'll look at your actual list, tell you straight whether it's worth working, and show you the AI employee running on real data. No pitch deck.

[Show me it working →](https://infinityreachmedia.com/book) [See what the leak is costing](https://infinityreachmedia.com/calculator)

Free, 15 minutes, and you keep the playbook either way.

Why speed is the whole game

The Four Leaks

## Every local business leaks money in the same four places

It doesn't matter whether you run a clinic, a gym, a law office, a repair shop, or a studio. The leaks are identical. Only the wording changes.

Leak 01 · The missed call

### Nobody picked up

The leak: you were with a customer, it was after hours, or it was lunch. The phone rang out, and they called the next name on the list.

An AI employee answers every call and message the moment it lands, day or night. It captures who they are and what they need, and books them if it can.

Leak 02 · The slow lead

### You replied the next morning

The leak: a form fill or DM at 8 PM that you saw at 9 AM. By then they'd already messaged three of your competitors.

The Speed to Lead AI employee replies in 60 seconds, asks the questions you'd ask, and puts qualified people straight on your calendar.

Leak 03 · The no show

### Booked isn't the same as showed

The leak: the appointment was on the books, nobody confirmed it, and the slot sat empty. You paid for that lead twice.

Automatic confirmations and reminders go out at the right moments, and cancellations get backfilled from your waitlist instead of vanishing.

Leak 04 · The dead list

### Your best customers forgot you exist

The leak: hundreds of past customers who liked your work and simply drifted. No reminder, no reason to come back.

The Dead List Miner runs campaigns to the list you already own. Revenue from people who already trust you, at nearly zero acquisition cost.

AI Employee 03 · Dead List Miner

AI Employee 04 · The Closer

### "Let me think about it" doesn't have to end there

The leak: someone goes quiet mid-conversation. You don't want to chase, chasing feels desperate, and a week later the thread is cold.

The AI employee stays in the conversation and handles the moment honestly: it asks what specifically they'd want to think over — usually one answerable thing — offers to hold a slot they can cancel by text, and books the second they're ready. It never pesters, and it stops the moment someone asks it to.

**Will it sound like me, or like a bot?**

**My list is small. Does this still work?**

The speed-to-lead and no-show AI employees work at any size, because they act on people already talking to you. The 10-appointment reactivation guarantee specifically needs at least 300 contacts with valid phone numbers — below that the math can't be honest. If your list is smaller, we'll tell you on the call rather than sell you a guarantee we can't stand behind.

No. The AI employees sit on top of what you already run and feed it. They answer the inquiry, qualify, and book into your existing calendar. You keep your tools, and your data stays in your accounts — always.

An onboarding call, access to your accounts, and approving messages until you're comfortable. We build, connect, and test everything before it touches a real prospect. Live in 7 days is in writing.

**Is this only for coaches with a group program?**

No. It fits any coach or consultant who sells from a conversation — one-to-one, group, mastermind, or done-for-you. If a booked call is how you make money, the AI employees fit.

**What does it cost?**

We price it on the call, once you've seen your own numbers — because what it's worth depends on what you're leaking and what a client is worth to you. Run the scorecard first if you'd rather have your figures before that conversation.

## Straight answers

**Is this compliant for insurance communication?**

The AI employees are configured around your carrier and state guidelines, and nothing sends without your approval until you choose to automate. We build conservative by default because our founder holds her own book and takes compliance as seriously as you do. Your compliance requirements always lead the setup.

**Will it sound like a robot to my clients?**

No. The AI employee is trained on your voice, your products, and your market. Clients get warm, human sounding texts. Complex questions get handed straight to you.

**I work my book myself. Why automate it?**

Because you can't text 400 households the week before their renewals while also running appointments. The AI employee does the outreach. You do the conversations that close. That's the division of labor that grows a book.

**How fast is setup?**

Seven days from signup to live. We connect your lead sources, your calendar, and your book, then test everything with you before it touches a real lead.

## Your next lead arrives tonight. Who's answering?

Book a free call. We'll look at your lead flow and your book, show you the AI employees live, and map exactly where the leaks close.

*About*

# I'm Yvette Kahn. My Team and I Build Every AI Employee.

Founder of Infinity Reach Media, out of Orange County. Twelve clients at a time, on purpose.

![Infinity Reach Media working session](https://infinityreachmedia.com/images/our-story.jpg)

*How This Started*

## I kept watching clients buy leads they already had.

Infinity Reach Media didn't start with ads. It started with organic content and follow-up systems that kept working after we logged off.

Then I noticed the same thing at almost every client. Customer lists worth thousands, sitting untouched. Calls ringing out while they did the actual work. And every one of them asking me to go buy more leads.

They didn't have a traffic problem. They had a follow-up problem. So I built the AI employees that go get that money back.

I've spent years writing marketing copy and building funnels. I don't have a computer science degree. I learned to build these because nobody was going to build them the way my clients actually needed them, and I got tired of waiting.

*How We Operate*

## Six rules I won't bend on.

Not values. Rules. Every one of them costs us something, which is how you know we mean them.

### Your data stays yours

We build inside your accounts, not a platform you have to rent access to. If you leave next month, you take everything with you. That's the point.

### You approve the sends

Approval mode is on from day one. Your AI employee drafts, you tap approve. You can switch it off once you trust it, but that's your call to make.

### Promises go in the contract

Three guarantees, written word for word into our terms — not just on a landing page. Live in 7 days. 60-second lead response. 10 booked appointments.

### Twelve clients. That's it.

Whoever scopes your build is whoever builds it and whoever picks up when something breaks. Capping the list is the only way that stays true.

### We built it, so we can fix it

These AI employees run on our own code, not a reseller kit with our logo on it. When you need something changed, we change it. We don't file a ticket with a vendor.

### We'll tell you not to buy

If five people a month contact you, an AI employee won't save you. If your close rate is the problem, more appointments won't fix it. We say so on the call.

*Who This Is For*

## Businesses that already have the customers.

The work only pays off if there's something to recover. Coaches whose best client started as a DM that sat for two days. Salons and med spas with a booking calendar full of gaps. Home services missing calls at 4:58 on a Friday. Insurance brokers sitting on a list they haven't touched in a year.

Every one of them was already earning that revenue. They were just losing it somewhere between the inquiry and the appointment.

If you're not sure that's you, don't take my word for it. [Run your own numbers](https://infinityreachmedia.com/scorecard) — it takes two minutes, it's free, and the report is yours whether we ever speak or not.

![Infinity Reach Media strategy session](https://infinityreachmedia.com/images/marketing-team.jpg)

title: "Getting Jessica Live in 7 Days | Infinity Reach Media"
description: "What happens after you say yes to Jessica — the day-by-day build, exactly what we need from you, and what stalls the clock. About 60 minutes of your time across seven days."

*Onboarding · Jessica, AI Sales Rep*

# You said yes. Here's every day of the next seven.

About 60 minutes of your time, total.

No project portal to learn, no eight-week discovery. You answer questions about your own business once, we build, you try to break her, she goes live.

If she isn't answering real leads by day seven, your setup fee comes back. That's in our [Terms](https://infinityreachmedia.com/terms), not in a sales deck.

*The build*

## Seven days, and you're only in four of them.

Pink days are yours. Gradient days are ours. The clock starts the moment your intake lands, not the moment you pay — so nothing is ticking while you're still gathering pricing.

Day
0

### You say yes

Agreement and setup fee go through in one link. Then you get exactly one thing back: the intake.

- Signed agreement and setup fee, both in the same email
- Your kickoff call booked inside 48 hours
- The intake link — one form, no login, save and come back

**Important**The seven-day clock starts when your intake is submitted, not at checkout. Take the weekend if you need it.

Day
1

### The intake — the only real homework

This is the whole job on your side. Everything Jessica knows about your business comes from this one form, so it's worth the 25 minutes. Full list is further down this page.

- Your services, in the words your customers actually use
- What she's allowed to quote, and what she must never quote
- The ten questions leads ask you every week, and the right answers
- Three texts you've sent a customer that sounded like you

**If you'd rather talk than type**Get on the kickoff call and we'll fill it in with you, live, while you talk. Most people find that faster.

[Open the intake form →](https://infinityreachmedia.com/jessica-intake)

Day
2

### Numbers and access

We set up the plumbing. Everything lives in accounts you own — if we ever part ways, you keep all of it, conversations included.

- A local number provisioned, or your existing line forwarded on no-answer
- Your calendar connected, with real buffers and real working hours
- Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp connected if you want those channels
- Compliance set up: opt-out language, consent capture, the required disclosures

**Your one job today**Approve the connection requests when they hit your phone. Takes about two minutes.

Day
3–4

### She learns your business

This is the part that makes her Jessica instead of a chatbot with your logo on it.

- Trained on your services, your pricing rules, your objections
- Booking logic wired to your real calendar, not a generic slot picker
- Escalation rules: what she must hand to a human, and how fast
- Her AI disclosure line, written in your voice — she says it on every first message
- The disqualifiers, so she stops wasting your time on leads you don't want

Day
5

### Test day — try to break her

You get a test number before any real lead ever touches her. This is the day people tell us they stopped being nervous.

- Text her like your worst lead. Push on price. Go quiet. Get rude.
- Paste in five real messages from past leads and see what she does
- Anything she gets wrong goes on a list and gets fixed the same day

**Nothing goes live without your yes**If test day doesn't satisfy you, we don't launch. We fix and retest.

Day
6

### Soft launch, one channel

She goes live on a single channel — usually text or web chat — and a human on our side reads every conversation that day. Not a sample. Every one.

- Real leads, one channel, full human review behind her
- Anything awkward gets corrected before it happens twice
- You get a short end-of-day note on what came in and what she did

Day
7

### Full launch

Every channel you approved is on. Leak one and leak two are plugged. The guarantee is met.

- All approved channels answering, one conversation per person across them
- Bookings landing on your calendar with reminders already scheduled
- Your team gets the handoff alerts, so nobody is guessing

Wk
2

### The week nobody else does

Week two is where a good AI employee becomes yours. We read transcripts daily and tighten her against what your real leads actually say.

- Daily transcript review, every weekday
- A Friday note: what she got wrong, what we changed, what's still open
- New FAQ answers added as your leads surface them

Day
30

### The number that decides everything

One call, real figures, no spin. You see what she did and you decide what happens next.

- Leads answered, and how fast she answered the first message
- Appointments booked, kept, and no-showed
- Conversations she escalated, and the ones she still can't handle
- Then you pick: more channels, the next AI employee, or stop here

*Your side of it*

## Every minute we'll ask you for.

Written down in advance, so nobody discovers a surprise workload in week two.

Day 0 — agreement and setup fee **10 min**

Day 1 — the intake form **25 min**

Day 2 — approve account connections **2 min**

Day 5 — test day, try to break her **20 min**

Day 30 — the results call **30 min**

**Total, across the first month** **87 min**

Anything not on this list, we do. You will not be asked to write scripts, build flows, learn a dashboard, or sit in a weekly status meeting.

*Day 1 in detail*

## What the intake actually asks.

Here it is in advance, so you can gather anything you don't have on hand. Most of it you already know by heart — it's the pricing rules that take people a minute.

#### Your services, in customer words

Not your internal names. What people type when they message you.

"AC not blowing cold" — not "diagnostic call-out"

#### Pricing rules

What she can say out loud, what's a range, and what has to wait for a human. This is the one that protects you.

"Can quote the $89 service call. Never quotes install."

#### Hours, service area, holidays

When you're open, how far you'll travel, and the days you're closed but leads still text.

She answers at 2am. She just won't promise you will.

#### Your calendar and its rules

Which calendar, how long a booking runs, travel buffers, and who owns which slot.

"90 min, 30 min drive buffer, never book Fridays after 3."

#### The ten questions you get every week

Your real FAQ, with the answers you'd give. This is the single biggest factor in how good she sounds.

"Do you take insurance?" "Are you licensed?" "How soon?"

#### Who you don't want

The leads that waste your day. She'll spot them and close them out politely instead of booking them.

Out of area, price shoppers, jobs you don't take

#### Escalation and handoff

Who she hands a live one to, how they get told, and how fast. Angry customers always go to a human.

"Text Mike within 5 minutes on anything over $5k."

#### Three texts that sound like you

Real messages you've sent a customer. She learns your voice from these, not from a tone slider.

Screenshots are fine. Copy and paste is fine.

*Straight talk*

## Three things that stall a build.

These are the only reasons a seven-day launch has ever slipped for us. All three are avoidable if you know about them on day zero.

**Undecided pricing rules**

By far the most common. If you haven't settled what she's allowed to quote, she can't answer the question every lead opens with. Decide this before day one and nothing else slows you down.

**Meta account access**

Instagram and Messenger need a Business account with you as admin. If yours is a personal profile, that conversion takes a day or two on Meta's side, not ours. We'll launch text and web chat first and add socials when it clears.

**No one to hand off to**

Jessica books appointments and escalates live ones. If nobody is on the other end of an escalation, she's answering into a void. We need one name and one number before launch.

**Live in 7 days** Counted from your intake, not your payment. Miss it and your setup fee comes back.

**Nothing launches without your yes** Test day is a real gate. If she doesn't satisfy you, we fix and retest before any lead sees her.

**Your accounts, your data** Number, calendar, conversations, contacts. All in accounts you own and keep.

Conditions in full in our [Terms of Service](https://infinityreachmedia.com/terms).

*Start*

## Want Jessica?

Talk to her first. Push on price, tell her you need to think about it, ask her whether she's a bot. If she handles you well, she'll handle your leads — and she'll book the call herself.

[Text Jessica: (714) 924-3024](sms:+17149243024?body=I%20want%20Jessica%20for%20my%20business) [Book the kickoff call](https://calendly.com/yvettekahn/30min)

We run twelve clients at a time on purpose. If we're full, we'll tell you that on the call and give you the date we open up — we won't take your setup fee and put you in a queue.

## 1. Acceptance of Terms

These Terms of Service ("Terms") govern your use of the website infinityreachmedia.com and any services provided by Infinity Reach Media ("we," "us," "our"). By engaging our services, submitting payment, or signing a service agreement, you ("Client," "you") agree to these Terms. If a signed service agreement between you and Infinity Reach Media conflicts with these Terms, the signed agreement controls. Our [Privacy Policy](https://infinityreachmedia.com/privacy) explains how we handle personal information and is incorporated into these Terms by reference.

## 2. Our Services

Infinity Reach Media provides digital marketing services including social media management, online advertising, email and SMS marketing, funnel design, coaching programs, and done for you AI employee systems for lead response, customer reactivation, review generation, and content ("AI Employee Suite"). The specific services, deliverables, timelines, and fees for your engagement are defined in your proposal, invoice, or signed service agreement.

## 3. Fees and Payment

Fees are due as stated in your proposal or invoice. Setup fees are due before work begins. Monthly service fees are billed in advance and are due on the same calendar day each month. We accept payment through our designated payment processors. Late payments beyond 7 days may result in a pause of services, including deactivation of AI employees, until the account is current. Third party costs such as advertising spend, software subscriptions in your name, and SMS carrier fees are your responsibility and are not refundable by us.

## 4. Guarantees and Refund Policy

We stand behind our AI Employee Suite with three written guarantees. Each guarantee has specific conditions, listed below, that exist so we can honor these promises for every client. Refunds under this section are the exclusive remedies for the matters they cover.

### 4.1 The Live in 7 Guarantee

If your AI employees are not built, tested, and live within 7 calendar days of your onboarding call, your setup fee will be refunded in full. The 7 day period begins on the date of your completed onboarding call, provided you have supplied the required access and materials described in Section 5. Days during which we are waiting on required Client access, approvals, or materials pause the 7 day clock and resume when the item is received. Refunds under this guarantee are issued to the original payment method within 10 business days of a written request to info@infinityreachmedia.com.

### 4.2 The 60 Second Promise

We track your Speed to Lead AI employee's response times continuously. If its average response time to new inbound leads exceeds 60 seconds across a full calendar month, your service fee for that month will be credited in full to your account, or refunded at your written request. This promise covers response time of the AI employee system itself. It does not cover delays caused by carrier filtering, platform outages of third party providers, leads submitted through channels not connected to the AI employee, or periods during which the Client has paused or disabled the AI employee or has unapproved messages pending beyond 24 hours.

### 4.3 The Leak Closed Guarantee

If the Dead List Miner does not generate at least 10 booked appointments from your existing customer list within the first 90 days of the AI employee going live, we will continue running and optimizing your reactivation campaigns at no additional service fee until the 10th appointment is booked. This guarantee is conditioned on the following:

"AI Employee" means an AI system we build, train, and operate for you; agreements and proposals that use the term "AI agent" refer to the same thing. "Dead List Miner" means the AI Employee that contacts your existing customer, client, or lead list, whatever it is called in your proposal or on the page you arrived from. This includes the AI employee previously named the Database Reactivation AI Employee, the Book Reactivation AI Employee, and the Rebooking Machine — a proposal naming any of those refers to the same AI employee and is covered by this guarantee.

1. Client provides a customer or lead list of at least 300 contacts with valid phone numbers before launch
2. Client approves pending campaign messages within 24 hours of notification
3. Client keeps calendar availability open for booking during the guarantee period
4. The guarantee is measured in booked appointments, not revenue, closed sales, or attended appointments, since attendance and closing are outside our control

### 4.4 General Refund Terms

1. Coaching programs, digital products, and completed one time projects such as funnel builds are non refundable once delivered, since the value is transferred at delivery. Where a written offer for a specific program includes its own guarantee, that written offer controls for that program.
2. Monthly retainer services may be cancelled with 30 days written notice. Fees already paid for the current billing period are not refundable except as provided by the guarantees above.
3. Refund requests must be submitted in writing to info@infinityreachmedia.com and will receive a response within 5 business days.
4. Approved refunds are issued to the original payment method within 10 business days.
5. Chargebacks filed without first requesting a refund through the process above are a breach of these Terms.

## 5. Client Responsibilities

Timelines and guarantees depend on your cooperation. You agree to provide, in a timely manner: access to required accounts and platforms, your customer or lead lists where applicable, brand materials, approvals of pending messages and content within 24 hours of notification, and accurate business information. You are responsible for the accuracy and lawful use of any contact list you provide, including having the necessary consent to contact those individuals by text, email, or phone under applicable laws such as the TCPA and CAN-SPAM. You retain final approval over messages sent on your behalf while approval mode is enabled, and you are responsible for compliance requirements specific to your industry, including insurance and financial services regulations.

## 6. Results Disclaimer

Except for the specific written guarantees in Section 4, we do not guarantee any particular business outcome, including revenue, closed sales, advertising performance, follower growth, or search rankings. Marketing results depend on factors outside our control, including your offer, pricing, sales process, market conditions, and platform algorithms. Testimonials and case studies on our website reflect individual experiences and are not a promise of similar results.

## 7. Intellectual Property

Upon full payment, you own the final deliverables created specifically for you, such as funnel copy, content, and creative assets. We retain ownership of our frameworks, systems, templates, prompts, AI employee configurations, and methodologies, including the I.N.C.O.M.E. Prompt-to-Profit System, and grant you a license to use them within your business for as long as your engagement or the applicable license remains active. You may not resell, share, or reproduce our frameworks, systems, or program materials.

## 8. Confidentiality and Data

We treat your business information, customer lists, and account credentials as confidential and use them only to deliver your services. We do not sell your data or your customers' data. Customer lists you provide remain your property and are returned or deleted at your written request upon termination. Our website and services may use third party processors for payments, scheduling, messaging, and analytics, each governed by their own privacy terms. Full detail, including text messaging consent and your privacy rights, is in our [Privacy Policy](https://infinityreachmedia.com/privacy).

## 9. Termination

Either party may terminate a monthly engagement with 30 days written notice. We may suspend or terminate services immediately for non payment, abusive conduct toward our team, unlawful use of the services, or use of contact lists without proper consent. Upon termination, AI employees and automations we operate for you are deactivated, and any amounts owed for services rendered become immediately due.

## 10. Limitation of Liability

To the maximum extent permitted by law, Infinity Reach Media's total liability arising out of or related to the services shall not exceed the amounts paid by you to us in the 3 months preceding the claim. We are not liable for indirect, incidental, consequential, or punitive damages, or for losses caused by third party platforms, carriers, or advertising networks. Nothing in these Terms limits liability that cannot be limited under applicable law.

## 11. Governing Law

These Terms are governed by the laws of the State of California. Any dispute shall be resolved in the state or federal courts located in Orange County, California, and the parties consent to that venue. Before filing any claim, the parties agree to attempt in good faith to resolve the dispute informally for 30 days.

## 12. SMS / Text Messaging Terms

Infinity Reach Media sends text messages in two programs: (a) messages about your own inquiry into our services, when you opt in on one of our forms or when you start the conversation yourself by texting a number we publish, such as (714) 924-3024 on our Jessica AI page; and (b) **transactional appointment messages sent on behalf of local businesses** that use our AI receptionist service — a booking confirmation, appointment reminders, and reschedule or cancellation notices, sent only after you verbally agree to receive them while booking by phone.

Message frequency varies by appointment activity. Message and data rates may apply. Reply **STOP** to opt out at any time or **HELP** for assistance. Consent to receive text messages is not a condition of purchasing any goods or services. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. See our [Privacy Policy](https://infinityreachmedia.com/privacy#sms) for how consent is collected and how mobile information is protected — it is never shared with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.

## 1. Who This Policy Covers

This Privacy Policy explains how Infinity Reach Media ("we," "us," "our") collects, uses, and protects information when you visit infinityreachmedia.com, submit a form, take our Revenue Leak Scorecard, book a call, or engage our services. It applies to information we collect about you directly. It does not change the terms of any signed service agreement. Our [Terms of Service](https://infinityreachmedia.com/terms) govern the services themselves.

## 2. Information We Collect

### 2.1 Information you give us

- **Contact details** — name, email address, phone number, business name, and website when you submit a form, take the scorecard, or book a call.
- **Business information** — the answers you provide in our scorecard and calculators, such as lead volume, average job value, and response times, which we use to generate your report.
- **Engagement information** — the account access, brand materials, and business details you provide when you become a client.

### 2.2 Information collected automatically

- **Usage data** — pages viewed, referring URL, approximate location derived from IP address, device and browser type, and the dates and times of your visits.
- **Advertising and analytics identifiers** — cookies and similar technologies set by the providers described in Section 5.

We do not collect Social Security numbers, government identification numbers, or payment card numbers on this website. Payments, when applicable, are processed by our payment processor, and we never receive or store your full card details.

## 3. How We Use Your Information

- To respond to your inquiry, deliver your scorecard or report, and schedule calls
- To provide, operate, and improve the services you engage us for
- To send you marketing communications by email or text, where you have consented, and which you can opt out of at any time
- To measure the performance of our advertising and website, including which ads and pages lead to inquiries
- To produce aggregated, de-identified benchmarks about how local businesses perform. These benchmarks never identify you or your business individually.
- To comply with legal obligations and enforce our Terms of Service

## 4. Text Messaging and Consent

There are three ways you may opt in to receive text messages from Infinity Reach Media:

**Online forms:** When you provide your phone number and check the consent box on one of our forms, you agree to receive text messages from Infinity Reach Media about your inquiry, your scorecard results, and our services.

**By texting us first:** When you send a text message to a number we publish, such as (714) 924-3024 on our Jessica AI page, you agree to receive text replies from Infinity Reach Media about your inquiry in that conversation. The disclosure next to the number states this, along with message and data rates, message frequency, and how to reply STOP or HELP.

**Verbally, when booking by phone:** Infinity Reach Media operates AI-powered phone receptionist services on behalf of local businesses. When you call a participating business and book, reschedule, or cancel an appointment, the receptionist asks whether you would like to receive a text confirmation and appointment reminders at the number you provide, and discloses that message and data rates may apply and that you can reply STOP at any time. If you agree on the call (which may be recorded), you consent to receive **transactional appointment messages only** for that booking — a booking confirmation, appointment reminders, and reschedule or cancellation notices, sent by Infinity Reach Media on behalf of the business you called. No marketing or promotional messages are sent under this opt-in.

Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply. Reply **STOP** to any message to opt out at any time, or **HELP** for help. Consent to receive texts is not a condition of purchasing any goods or services. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.

**We do not share mobile information with third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.** All of the sharing categories described in Section 6 exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; that information is not shared with any third parties.

## 5. Cookies and Advertising

We use cookies and similar technologies to understand how the site is used and to measure our advertising. These may include:

- **Analytics** — to see which pages and sources produce inquiries.
- **Advertising** — including Google Ads and Meta (Facebook and Instagram) technologies, which allow us to measure ad performance and to show ads to people who have visited our site. This is commonly called remarketing.

You can control cookies through your browser settings. You can opt out of personalized Google advertising at [adssettings.google.com](https://adssettings.google.com/), out of Meta ad personalization in your Facebook or Instagram ad preferences, and out of many other participating networks at [optout.aboutads.info](https://optout.aboutads.info/). We honor Global Privacy Control signals where required by law.

## 6. How We Share Information

**We do not sell your personal information.** We share information only in these situations:

- **Service providers** that operate our business under contract, including website hosting, scheduling, email and messaging delivery, customer relationship management, analytics, advertising measurement, and payment processing. They may use your information only to perform services for us.
- **Legal requirements** — when required by law, subpoena, or to protect our rights, safety, or property.
- **Business transfer** — if our business is merged or acquired, information may transfer as part of that transaction, subject to this policy.

As stated in Section 4, text messaging opt-in data and consent are excluded from all sharing above and are never shared with third parties.

## 7. Data We Handle for Clients

When you engage us as a client, you may provide customer or lead lists so our AI employees can contact them on your behalf. In that situation you are the controller of that data and we act as your service provider. We use it only to deliver your services, we do not sell it, and we do not use it to market our own business. Your lists remain your property and are returned or deleted at your written request when your engagement ends. You are responsible for having the legal right and consent to contact the individuals on any list you provide, as described in our [Terms of Service](https://infinityreachmedia.com/terms#client).

## 8. Retention and Security

We keep personal information only as long as needed for the purposes described here, to meet legal and tax obligations, and to resolve disputes. Inquiry and scorecard data is generally retained for up to 24 months unless you ask us to delete it sooner. Client engagement records are retained for the length of the engagement plus the period required by law.

We use commercially reasonable safeguards to protect information, including access controls on the systems that hold client data. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

## 9. Your Privacy Rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to request access to the personal information we hold about you, to request correction or deletion of it, to opt out of marketing communications, and to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information for targeted advertising.

### California residents

Under the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended, you may request disclosure of the categories and specific pieces of personal information we have collected, request deletion or correction, and opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information. **We do not sell personal information and we do not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising beyond the advertising measurement described in Section 5.** We will not discriminate against you for exercising these rights. To make a request, email [info@infinityreachmedia.com](mailto:info@infinityreachmedia.com) with the subject line "Privacy Request." We will verify your identity and respond within 45 days.

To stop marketing emails, use the unsubscribe link in any email. To stop text messages, reply STOP.

## 10. Children's Privacy

Our website and services are intended for businesses and adults. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 16. If you believe a child has provided us information, contact us and we will delete it.

## 11. Changes to This Policy

We may update this policy from time to time. The current version is always posted on this page with the updated date shown above. Material changes will be communicated to active clients directly.

## 12. Contact Us

Questions or privacy requests: [info@infinityreachmedia.com](mailto:info@infinityreachmedia.com)

Infinity Reach Media · Orange County, California


---
title: "Accessibility Statement | Infinity Reach Media"
description: "Infinity Reach Media's commitment to making infinityreachmedia.com usable by everyone, the standard we work to, known limitations, and how to report a barrier."
url: "https://infinityreachmedia.com/accessibility"
---

## Our commitment

Infinity Reach Media is working to make infinityreachmedia.com usable by as many people as possible, including people who browse with a screen reader, navigate by keyboard alone, use voice control, or rely on magnification or high-contrast settings. We treat accessibility as part of building the site, not a box to tick afterwards.

## The standard we work to

We aim to meet the **Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA**. These are the guidelines referenced by the Americans with Disabilities Act and by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services for the health-sector deadline in May 2027.

## What we have done

- Body text meets or exceeds the 4.5:1 contrast minimum against its background, and most of the site now exceeds the stricter 7:1 AAA threshold.
- Every form field has a label programmatically associated with it, required fields are marked with a visible asterisk and announced as required, and validation errors name the specific field and what to correct.
- The site can be operated by keyboard alone, with a visible focus indicator and a skip link to jump past the navigation.
- Navigation collapses to a labelled menu button on small screens, and that button reports whether the menu is open.
- Pages use real landmarks and a single descriptive heading order so assistive technology can navigate structurally.
- Images carry alternative text, and decorative images are hidden from assistive technology.

## Known limitations

We would rather name these than imply the site is perfect:

- Some pages embed third-party tools — a Calendly scheduler and a live chat agent. We do not control their markup and cannot guarantee they meet AA. If one of them blocks you, email or text us and we will complete the same task with you directly.
- Video testimonials on our reviews page are hosted on third-party players. Captions depend on that platform.
- We are continuing to audit older landing pages and fix issues as we find them.

## Tell us about a barrier

If any part of this site stops you from doing what you came to do, we want to know, and we will help you complete it another way in the meantime.

- Email: [info@infinityreachmedia.com](mailto:info@infinityreachmedia.com)
- Text or call: [(714) 924-3024](tel:+17149243024)

We aim to reply within one business day. Please tell us the page, what you were trying to do, and the assistive technology or browser you were using, and we will reproduce it from there.

## Formal approach

This statement reflects our current, good-faith assessment of the site. It is not a legal guarantee of conformance. We review it when the site changes materially and at least once a year.
